about: Bespoke HD-2D map improvements. Each sheet's sprites are in reading order; imported by landmarks.py. Generated with image_gen, 2026-11-14. Existing named works keep their M7 artwork. Mana nodes share an intentional family with school-coloured runtime light.

sheets.name: monuments
sheets.prompt: Create a production sprite sheet for Fall from Heaven HD-2D fantasy strategy game. EXACTLY NINE different isolated map-object sprites on a regular 3 by 3 grid, in reading order, one object per equal square cell with generous transparent gutters. Transparent background. Full object in each cell, no clipping, no text, no captions, no grid lines. Chunky crisp 16-bit PIXEL ART with visibly deliberate pixel clusters, limited muted earthy olive/brown/slate palette, dark one-pixel outlines, strong upper-left highlights and shadow on lower-right. Three-quarter view looking down about 35 degrees at the front of the objects, consistent scale and lighting. Small-map readability, bold distinctive silhouettes, sculpted details, no photographic texture, no anti-aliased painterly blur, no mist or bloom. Objects stand independently with no terrain tile or cast shadow. Draw exactly these nine objects, left to right across rows: a colossal weathered stone giant standing guard with small gargoyles nesting in carved shoulder alcoves (Guardian of Pristin Pass); a half-buried petrified winged warrior archangel trapped in jagged rock (Odio's Prison); an enormous bleached dragon skull with a curved ribcage and spine; a cluster of ancient jade-green imperial statues on broken plinths (Remnants of Patria); a cracked open gothic sepulcher with its shattered sealing stone and exposed dark stairway; an open white-stone sarcophagus shrine entwined in fresh green vines (Tomb of Sucellus); a shattered frozen throne and sword embedded in blue-white ice (Letum Frigus); a ring of pale starlight standing stones imprisoning a tiny fiery winged angel (Ring of Carcer); a white stone stepped pyre with golden angel wings and holy fire (Pyre of the Seraphic)
